hachette.title: The Nervous System Reset
hachette.author: Jessica Maguire
hachette.description: “The Nervous System Reset fills in the blanks left by typical methods of healing. This book is the missing ingredient that so many people have searched for.”

hachette.title: Skully’s Best Día Ever!
hachette.author: Rhode Montijo
hachette.description: Come on a rambunctious adventure and explore a vibrant Dí​a de los Muertos-inspired town alongside Skully the skeleton, who sets out on a hilarious quest to have the perfect day!

hachette.title: A Lovely and Deadly Dance
hachette.author: Claire Andrews
hachette.description: Something is stalking the queen of England, and Irene Adler is ready to find whatever monster may lurk behind this new gruesome string of murders—with or without the help of Sherlock Holmes.

hachette.title: Holly Black’s Isles of Elfhame 1,000-Piece Puzzle
hachette.author: Holly Black
hachette.description: Holly Black is the #1 New York Times bestselling author of fantasy books, including the novels of Elfhame, The Coldest Girl in Coldtown, The Spiderwick Chronicles, and her adult duology, Book of Night and Thief of Night. She has been a finalist for an Eisner Award and the Lodestar Award and the recipient of the Mythopoeic Award, a Nebula, and a Newbery Honor. Her books have been translated into 32 languages worldwide and adapted for film and television. She currently lives in New England with her family in a house with a secret library. She invites you to visit her online at blackholly.com or on Instagram @blackholly.

hachette.title: Holly Black’s Faerie Coloring Postcards
hachette.author: Holly Black
hachette.description: 50 postcards for coloring in and sharing with friends or displaying, featuring gorgeous original line art of characters and scenes from the fantastical Faerie world of #1 New York Times bestselling author Holly Black, including The Cruel Prince, The Stolen Heir, and the rest of her beloved series.

hachette.title: Holly Black’s Faerie Tarot Deck and Guidebook
hachette.author: Holly Black
hachette.description: A one-of-a-kind, gold-foiled, deluxe tarot deck and guidebook set that reimagines the classic cards to offer passage into the Faerie realm, from #1 New York Times bestselling author Holly Black (The Cruel Prince, The Stolen Heir). Just beyond our own world is Elfhame, the land of Faerie, where the capricious and dangerous Folk dwell. Mortals may journey there if they are clever—or foolish—enough to find the way. Often, they return with blessings or curses, but always with new wisdom. Let these cards be your allies as you solve riddles, determine whom you can trust, and forge a path to victory (perhaps even snagging a crown in the process). This set includes:

hachette.title: The Little Frog Matching Game
hachette.author: Maybell Eequay
hachette.description: Relax and have a little fun with your favorite amphibian by matching 25 pairs in this sweet and simple memory game!

hachette.title: The Little Frog 1,000-Piece Puzzle
hachette.author: Maybell Eequay
hachette.description: The Little Frog inhabits a cozy world of soothing scenery, and they explore it all while wearing an endless collection of stylish shoes! With this high-quality, 1,000-piece jigsaw puzzle, you can join this adorable amphibian in a mindful activity that takes you on adventure across land, pond, and sky.

hachette.title: Bad Naturalist
hachette.author: Paula Whyman
hachette.description: With humor, humility, and awe, one woman attempts to restore 200 acres of farmland long gone-to-seed in the Blue Ridge Mountains, facing her own limitations while getting to know a breathtaking corner of the natural world.

hachette.title: The Eclectic World of Julia Rothman Wrapping Paper Book
hachette.author: Julia Rothman
hachette.description: Julia Rothman is a highly acclaimed contemporary illustrator and author of many best-selling books, including Nature Anatomy, Farm Anatomy, Ocean Anatomy, Food Anatomy, Nature Anatomy Notebook, Wildlife Anatomy, Insect Anatomy, and Bird Anatomy. Her illustrated column, Scratch, ran for five years in the Sunday New York Times. Clients for her illustrations and pattern designs include Target, The Washington Post, MTA Arts & Design, and more. She lives and works in Brooklyn, New York.

hachette.title: A Summer of Stars
hachette.author: Liana Cincotti
hachette.description: Liana Cincotti lives in New England and works in marketing. She strives to bring back the magic found in iconic early 2000s romantic comedies. When she's not writing, you can find her curled up in her reading chair watching the newest sitcom, devouring a cookies and cream milkshake.

hachette.title: The Brothers Karamazov
hachette.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
hachette.description: Fyodor Dostoevsky (1821–1881) was a novelist, short story writer, and journalist. Widely regarded as one of the greatest novelists ever, his most acclaimed novels—Crime and Punishment, The Brothers Karamazov, and The Idiot—have had an immeasurable impact on world literature, Existentialism, and Freudian psychology.

hachette.title: Moon Puerto Rico
hachette.author: Suzanne Van Atten
hachette.description: Suzanne Van Atten has written about destinations throughout the United States, Mexico, South America, the Caribbean, and Europe. She has barhopped in Barcelona, slept in a Jesuit monastery on the Amalfi coast, crewed a hot air balloon in New Mexico, gone white-water rafting in Tennessee, and gotten lost too many times to count. Amidst all these travels, she always returns to Puerto Rico, a place she fell in love with when she lived there as a teenager. The country's rich culture, postcard-perfect beaches, lush tropical jungle, cobblestone streets, pastel colors, lively music, and the joie de vivre of its people colluded to seduce her. No matter how many times she returns, she always discovers something new and delightful. Suzanne is a freelance writer and editor based in Los Angeles.

hachette.title: How to Train Your Dragon School: Fight of the Flamestrike
hachette.author: Cressida Cowell
hachette.description: Cressida Cowell is the bestselling author of The Wizards of Once and the How to Train Your Dragon series. She grew up in London and on a small, uninhabited island off the west coast of Scotland, where she spent her time writing stories, fishing for things to eat, and exploring the island. She now lives in Hammersmith, England, with her husband, three children, and a dog named Pigeon.

hachette.title: The Nobody Code
hachette.author: Miciah Bay Gault
hachette.description: Miciah Bay Gault has an MFA in Fiction from Syracuse. She teaches in the MFA program at VCFA and directs the Vermont Book Award. Miciah’s work has appeared in the New York Times, Tin House, LitHub, Electric Literature, the Harvard Review, and many others. She’s been a fellow at Bread Loaf, a Visiting Writer at the Vermont Studio Center, and the recipient of a Vermont Arts Council Creation Grant.

hachette.title: A Hard Habit to Break
hachette.author: Siera London
hachette.description: Siera London is the USA Today Bestselling & Award-winning author of contemporary and paranormal romance, romantic suspense, and crime fiction. She crafts stories of diverse characters navigating the challenges and triumphs to find lasting love. Intelligence, wit, emotion, drama, and romance are between the covers of every Siera London novel. Siera lives in Virginia with her husband, and a color patch tabby named Frie. Also, Siera is a Director-At-Large for Romance Writers of America.

hachette.title: The Inevitable Undoing of Zahara Douglass
hachette.author: Leslye Penelope
hachette.description: “Another captivating, unforgettable work of art.” ―Clarence A. Haynes, author of The Broken Hearts Agency

hachette.title: Tendrils
hachette.author: Carrie Harris
hachette.description: Carrie Harris writes both original and licensed books in a variety of worlds including Marvel, Warhammer 40k, the World of Darkness, and the Fate RPG. Over her 20+ years in the industry, Carrie has coached many aspiring authors, most notably as a former organizer of WriteOnCon, an online kidlit writing conference. She is a member of the International Association of Media Tie-In Writers and the Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association. In her spare time, Carrie often appears on podcasts and at conventions to gush at length about her favorite fandoms. A former tabletop game exec, she can’t say no to a game night invitation, especially for coop games and classic dungeon crawlers. She enjoys crafts like crocheting and cross stitch and learned how to cook from a real French chef. Carrie lives just outside NYC with her ninja doctor husband, three teenagers, and a cranky dog named Slartibartfast.

hachette.title: The Dungeon Book
hachette.author: Gareth Hanrahan
hachette.description: Gareth Hanrahan's three-month break from computer programming to concentrate on writing has now lasted fifteen years and counting. He's written more gaming books than he can readily recall, by virtue of the alchemical transmutation of tea and guilt into words. He lives in Ireland with his wife and three children. Follow him on Twitter at @mytholder.

hachette.title: Freight
hachette.author: Ryan Lowell
hachette.description: Ryan Lowell’s fiction has appeared in Portland Monthly Magazine, Worker’s Write Journal and other publications. His story “Things Fall Apart” was a Glimmer Train short story award contest finalist. Freight is his first novel. He lives in South Portland, Maine, with his wife and two sons.

hachette.title: Babies
hachette.author: Dan Kainen
hachette.description: The bestselling, eye-opening Photicular series goes majorly cute with baby animals in irresistible living motion. The bestselling Photicular series just got a cuteness injection with BABIES. Using an innovative lenticular-based technology, precision sliding lenses, and four-color video imagery, each image is like a 3D movie on the page, delivering a rich, fluid, immersive visual experience. A litter of puppies dash through the grass. A lion cub practices its roar. A mama horse and foal go for a gallop. A little chimpanzee gleefully bangs about. A sea lion pup lounges in the sun. Also featuring a penguin chick, mama bear and cub, and elephant calf. Through an introductory essay and animal profiles by science writer Mara Grunbaum, and amazing—and adorable—moving images of baby animals, readers will learn about how young animals in the wild sharpen their instincts, build bonds, and learn to survive.

hachette.title: Anna Karenina
hachette.author: Leo Tolstoy
hachette.description: Count Leo Tolstoy (1828-1910) was born to a noble Russian family and produced some of the most outstanding works of realist fiction, including Anna Karenina, War and Peace, and The Death of Ivan Ilyich. Tolstoy was also an advocate of democratic education, Christian anarchism, pacificism, and vegetarianism.

hachette.title: Three Little Witches and the Spooky Old House
hachette.author: Peggy Archer
hachette.description: Peggy Archer is an author of fiction, poetry, and nonfiction for children. Her picture book A Hippy-Hoppy Toad was a Junior Library Guild Gold Standard Selection, a Bank Street College of Education Best Children’s Book of the Year, and a winner of the SCBWI Crystal Kite Award. She lives in Valparaiso, Indiana, with her husband and invites you to visit her online at peggyarcher.com.Gaia Bordicchia is a graduate of the IED (Istituto Europeo di Design/European Institute of Design) and has illustrated numerous children’s books, including The Amazing Animal Atlas by Nick Crumpton. Her first book as an author-illustrator, La forêt des Lanternes, was published in France in 2018. Based in northern Italy, Gaia invites you to visit her online at lagaia.art.

hachette.title: Sheet Cakes!
hachette.author: Zola Gregory
hachette.description: Zola Gregory is a writer, recipe developer, and food stylist based in Seattle. Her work has appeared in publications such as TASTE, Food52, Bon Appétit, and Serious Eats. Zola has worked professionally as a pastry chef and baker, she now enjoys helping others find success in their own kitchens through her stories, recipes, and baking classes.
